title: Product 02 revision 2 independent PDF review
source: Five actual Product 02 PDFs regenerated from the remote-confirmed source SHA using issueReport(); every Q4/Q5 answer was read and rescored. The other 25 blocks were text-compared to the preceding scored PDF and retained their prior rubric scores because their extracted answer text was identical.
method: Manual six-part rubric. All 35 current PDF answer texts were extracted. Changed Q4/Q5 answers were rescored; unchanged 25 answers were compared byte-for-byte after PDF text normalization and retained the previous manual scoring. Profile means are the arithmetic mean of seven answer totals rounded to one decimal. Automated diagnostics are not content scores.

answerRecords.questionTitle: Which careers suit me best?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Business development, sales or account growth matches your chart's emphasis on finding customers and openings. What This Means for You: A role with room to build relationships and act on an opportunity fits you. A system that adds sales targets without control over delivery creates a sharper mismatch. Bottom Line: Customer growth fits best when delivery stays within your control.
answerRecords.deductionReason: Strong direct role fit and useful job-condition detail; the examples are still role families rather than a tailored occupation, and some practical wording is shared with later answers.

answerRecords.questionTitle: Am I better suited to employment or independent work?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Structured employment is better supported by the chart. What This Means for You: For a structured job, your chart shows training or specialist support. For independent work, a customer-income marker appears, but the chart does not show a complete link from useful work to paid customers.
answerRecords.deductionReason: The employment-versus-independent conclusion is clear and chart-supported, but the explanation repeats the same job-setting evidence and does not compare actual pay or work conditions.

answerRecords.questionTitle: How do I naturally make money?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Your income pattern has two routes: regular pay or repeat work, and additional income from projects or new customers. Both appear in your chart, rather than a single fixed earning style. What This Means for You: Customer or project income is linked to day-to-day work and shared commitments. Steady pay is linked to your wider network and day-to-day work. These are possible earning routes, not expected pay. Bottom Line: Your chart supports a dependable base plus a second route through projects or customers.
answerRecords.deductionReason: The text accurately states the money route and limits. Where the chart only has a limited, hidden sign, it names a possible route but gives little usable explanation of how that route relates to the customer’s work pattern.

answerRecords.questionTitle: What tends to block my financial progress?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Your chart links income-related effort with learning or support. This may create a time or cost pressure, but the chart cannot confirm that it is limiting your finances.
answerRecords.deductionReason: A single answer now states the chart-linked pressure and uncertainty without a repeated explanation or bottom line. It remains cautious and cannot verify that this is a real-world cause.
